angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 28,025,579 km at 116.55 pc = 3.21 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 85670: distance 116.55 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.012), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 116.55 +/- 1.399 pc; Gaia DR3 cannot see the star
radiusSource: Radius 40.284 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 85670: radius 40.284 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 996.471 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.05) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 28,025,579 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 5113 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 85670: effective temperature 5113 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.049) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 85670: effective temperature 5113 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.049) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * bet Dra: spectral type G2Ib-IIa (1989ApJS...71..245K)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * bet Dra: projected rotation speed 6.76 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2024A&A...692A.189R)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (HST/STIS Next Generation Spectral Library v2 (Heap & Lindler; MAST high-level science product), HD 159181) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 2.05 from 2024A&A...692A.189R; the 24 published values span log g 1.35 to 2.05, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.6% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...692A.189R)
